No opt-out flag should be added, because three escape hatches already exist and each is reached by naming something rather than by setting a flag. `look_path` opens any single named file, including one inside a snapshot, and is untouched by this design. `look --grep` rooted at a path that is itself tetel content passes no exclusions at all, which is not merely permitted but forced: grep's `--exclude-dir` suppresses a directory named as the recursion root, so the flags must be withheld there or naming a snapshot directory would return nothing. And `run` spawns `argv` directly with nothing between the empty-argv refusal and the spawn that inspects, parses or classifies the command or the paths it will touch, so it has no place a path exclusion could be applied even in principle. A flag would add a fourth route that, unlike all three of these, leaves no trace in what was named.

Every evidence record already stores a pin — on the witnessed path the pin of the grounder's own fact, i.e. the tree it stood in, written expressly so that "was this claim graded against the same tree the memo was written against?" becomes measurable — in a field no check reads today; so rule 3 is implementable as a comparison of that stored pin against the claim's currently stated pin, answerable on ledgers already written, whereas folding the pin into `sha256_hex` would change every pinned claim's current digest and drive every previously written record into `out_of_proof`.

The donor's self-citation exclusion is not needed at the destination: check 5 skips a self-edge so that a root is "never reported as its own dependent", whereas the owed closure's output is a set of ids to grade that already contains its own seeds, so a self-edge can only re-derive owed-ness a claim already has and changes neither the set nor its termination.

The bound earns its own `NON_COVERAGE` line rather than being folded into an existing one. The list already discriminates a withholding tetel chose (the tetel-output exclusion) from platform accidents that "contemplate nothing tetel chose" (grep skipping symlinked directories and binary files); a bound tetel applies to its own return is of the first kind. What the line states is a gap `check` genuinely cannot close: a fact's extent records the whole search, and nothing anywhere establishes that the author read all of it — `scope.rs` names that limit as permanently out of reach and does not claim otherwise.

The `prose-revised-since-proof` listing is a pure function of three recomputed quantities and stores none of them: a block's current (text, cite-list) pair, the timestamp at which that exact pair first appeared in the block's event history, and an anchor equal to the maximum over the block's cited claims of each claim's earliest non-refuting record whose proposition digest matches the claim's current wording. The block is listed exactly when the pair's first-appearance timestamp exceeds the anchor, and is skipped outright when it is a heading, when its current cite-list is empty, or when no cited claim has such a record.

A sibling `acks.jsonl`, added to `snapshot::SNAPSHOT_FILES`, degrades safely in the older build it will be shipped past: that constant is an explicit enumeration whose stated purpose is that a future workspace file be a deliberate decision to ship or withhold, so a build that predates the entry simply never opens the file, reads `prose.jsonl` unchanged, and reproduces TET-30's un-suppressed listing. The owed predicate as decided here: a claim is owed iff it is in `analyze_ledger`'s `ungrounded_claims`, or in its `out_of_proof`, or the pin stored on its records differs from the memo's currently stated pin, or fewer than N distinct non-author workspaces have a record whose `proposition_digest` equals the current proposition's, or `citation_ids_in` finds in its proposition text the id of a claim that is itself owed — the last computed to a fixpoint. prop: The bound cannot be derived from the caller's cap: the MCP `look` handler receives no field carrying one and returns `printed` unmeasured, so any number tetel applies is chosen by a person. Following this crate's own handling of an arbitrary number — `describe_buffer`, which refuses to invent a staleness threshold on the grounds that "a number chosen here would be arbitrary" and reports instead — the constant must be documented as a judgement and the design's load must rest on the report, not on the number.

Hitting the bound must not be an error at the destination: `look_grep` returns the bounded text as a successful `LookOutcome` exactly as it returns a whole one, and records the shortfall in the label rather than refusing. This follows the crate's own report-rather-than-refuse handling of an arbitrary number in `describe_buffer`, and it is forced anyway — the pending entries are already written from the full stdout by the time any bound is applied, so a refusal would have to discard a capture that already happened.

The bound cannot disturb observation identity at the destination: the `Search` entry is keyed by `search_key(root_path, &m.root)` and each per-file entry by `resolve_key(Path::new(&file))`, both computed from paths alone, so two searches of the same root for the same pattern overlap each other whether either was bounded or not.

The `NON_COVERAGE` entry must carry the general statement only, with the per-search numbers left to the label, because every string in that list is static and none is per-search. This is exactly the division TET-46 already made for exclusions: the static list says a census reports the tree minus what tetel withheld, and each search's own label names what that particular search withheld, which is what a reader of the Facts table sees.

An acknowledged block must still print, not vanish. Deleting the entry would make "no post-proof prose revision exists in this memo" and "one exists and a human has read it against its claims" indistinguishable in the check report, whereas this crate treats distinguishable states as owed distinct output — its no-rows path says so in as many words, that being "a distinct state from a clean run, not a weaker way of spelling it". Printing also costs nothing the residue does not already pay: the entry format already carries an author's own `--why` verbatim under `revised because:`, with the source comment stating that it is never a paraphrase and is the most actionable thing the entry can hand a reader.

The acknowledgement is a strict filter over the trigger's output, applied after `prose_after_proof` has produced its list, and therefore cannot add a listing that TET-30 would not have produced — a stale, malformed or unmatched ack simply fails to suppress, which is the same state as no ack at all. Two consequences hold without further argument: the set of blocks the reader is asked to act on is always a subset of TET-30's, so no new false demand can be manufactured; and `machine_check_failed` is untouched, since `prose_revised_since_proof` is not among its disjuncts and the ack changes only which entries populate it. It also follows that the digest component does not close any part of TET-30's conceded non-coverage for prose that ships alongside a claim revision — it only stops an acknowledgement outliving the state it attested to.

An acknowledged block should leave the `prose-revised-since-proof` group and be printed instead under one collapsed document-level bullet carrying, per acknowledged block, its id, its document line, its acknowledgement timestamp and the author's `--why` verbatim. This is the shape the crate already reaches for: the residue's own preamble is one document-level bullet, and the comment justifying it names `ledger_has_no_scope_columns` as precedent on the ground that a constant repeated per row buries the findings that are about this document. Leaving the block inside the demanding group with an extra annotation would keep a standing demand a human has already discharged, which is the skim-training failure the design exists to remove; removing it from the report entirely is refused by the preceding claim.

The minting surface is one verb, `tetel prose --ack <id> --why <text>` with the matching MCP argument pair, built as a variant of the single request shape both front ends already share so the two cannot drift on which missing flag is refused. Its refusals are exactly the workspace-decidable ones the existing prose verbs use, raised through the same `workspace::refuse` helper: no such block, the block is a heading, the block carries no citations, a cited id that does not resolve to a claim in `claims.jsonl`, and an empty `--why` — the last on the identical `why.trim().is_empty()` test that already backs "--revise requires --why (revisions must explain themselves)". None inspects the content or plausibility of the reason. The verb cannot refuse an ack on a block that is not currently listed, because an authoring workspace holds no evidence records at all — they live beside the rendered memo — so it cannot compute an anchor; and it need not, since an ack on an unlisted block suppresses nothing.

The acknowledgement event cannot live in `prose.jsonl`. `ProseEvent` is an internally-tagged serde enum over exactly `Create` and `Revise`, and `workspace::read_jsonl` propagates any line's parse failure as an error over the whole log rather than skipping it; empirically, a build at this pin reading a `prose.jsonl` containing one valid `Create` line and one `{"event":"Ack",...}` line fails the entire read with `unknown variant \`Ack\`, expected \`Create\` or \`Revise\`` and exits 1. A new tag value therefore makes every older build unable to read even the prose it already understood.

An acknowledgement must not enter `render`'s output. Keeping the rendered bytes a function of facts, claims, prose, targets and transplants only — with `acks.jsonl` shipped by the snapshot copy loop but never read by `compose::render` — preserves the determinism the provenance-drift finding rests on, and buys a property that makes the required re-render honest rather than merely tolerable: re-rendering after an ack and nothing else rewrites the snapshot in place, since existing snapshot files are overwritten, while leaving the memo byte-identical. The discharge therefore shows up in version control as a change to the record and no change to the argument, which is exactly what it is.

Supersession needs no verb and withdrawal needs one, and both are resolved by log order rather than by timestamp. Supersession is automatic: since suppression is existential over matching keys, a later ack with a different key simply fails to match and a duplicate ack for the same key changes nothing. Withdrawal is a second event, `Unack`, carrying a block id and its own required verbatim `--why`; suppression then requires a key-matching ack appended after the last `Unack` for that block. Naming only the block, rather than a key, is sufficient because a key-mismatched ack is already void. Resolving by position in an append-only log written one line per event, rather than by comparing timestamps, keeps the whole acknowledgement mechanism free of clock comparisons. Withdrawal has to exist: without it, an author who acknowledged in error and cannot yet rewrite the paragraph would have no honest act available — which is precisely the defect this design was written to remove, reproduced one level up.

prop: Three invalidation invariants follow from the key, each with the mutation that reddens its test. (i) Any later change to the block's text or to its citation list voids the ack, because both are components of the key; the mutation is to compare only the text, after which a citation-only revision — which TET-30's C6 records as an act that lists rather than clears — would stay suppressed. (ii) Any change to a cited claim's proposition voids the ack, because the key carries that claim's proposition digest; the mutation is to drop the digest set from the key, after which an ack would outlive a rewrite of the very claim the author read the paragraph against. (iii) A workspace with no `acks.jsonl` produces byte-identical output to today's, because `workspace::read_jsonl` treats a missing file as an empty log rather than an error; the mutation is to make the missing file an error, after which every memo rendered before this design existed would fail to check.

For a claims-unaffected prose edit — a typo or wording fix that leaves every cited claim's proposition untouched — both of TET-30's two clearing acts misrepresent what the author did. Restoring the text and citation list, which C6 names as the first act, restores the defect the edit corrected. Revising or adding a cited claim and having the new wording graded, C6's second act, requires changing a claim that is correct; and because `out_of_proof` is one of the disjuncts of `Findings::machine_check_failed` while `prose_revised_since_proof` is not, that route drives the run to a machine failure until a further grounding pass lands, spending a red check and a pass to silence a line that never failed the run.

The sketch's second suppression clause — that the ack's timestamp be later than the recomputed anchor — is dropped, because it cannot fire. The rule is only consulted for a block the trigger already listed, and listing means the current pair's first-appearance timestamp already exceeds the anchor; an ack recording that same current pair is appended to an append-only log by the same authoring workspace, after that pair exists, and stamped by the same `workspace::now_unix()` that stamped the prose event. So unless the authoring machine's clock runs backwards between the two appends, the ack's timestamp exceeds the block timestamp which already exceeds the anchor, and the clause is satisfied in every case it is evaluated. Dropping it leaves the suppression predicate free of any timestamp comparison at all, which is why — unlike the trigger it guards — the acknowledgement does not rest on two clocks agreeing.

Portability, not privacy, is what justifies this change, and privacy must not be promised. After a capture-time label change a committed artifact still carries machine-local paths in author-typed claim propositions, in `proc:` command lines and their keys, in every extent `key`, and in `predicate.world[].root` — 901 occurrences of the last across the eight committed evidence ledgers alone.

Recording "showed N of M" in the label does not violate the crate's "nothing derived is stored" rule. That rule is stated as a reason to recompute values a re-run can obtain from the shipped ledger, and the shown-count is not one of them: the `Search` entry's `output` is empty and the per-file entries record what was captured, not how much of it was returned, so how much the author was shown is unrecoverable from the ledger after the fact. It is an event, and recording it is the only way it survives.

Two entries are owed in `NON_COVERAGE`, by the list's own stated standard that a deliberate exclusion earns its own line because a refusal that fired is easily read as coverage it never claimed. First: that an acknowledgement records only that a human said they re-read the paragraph against its claims, and that nothing verifies the reading happened or judges whether the paragraph is faithful — the tool's silence after an ack is the author's assertion, not the tool's finding. Second: that an acknowledgement minted after the last `render --out` is not in the snapshot the check reads, so it does not suppress anything until the memo is re-rendered. Both are static general statements, which is the only form entries in this constant can take.

prop: This design knowingly breaks both halves of TET-30's C11 sentence "Nothing new ships in the snapshot, no schema changes": a tenth file ships, and a new event schema exists. The price is bounded and should be stated rather than absorbed. `check` always prints the binary that produced a report, on the stated ground that a report which does not name its build cannot be disbelieved, so two reports disagreeing about one memo's residue can be attributed to their checkers — which is sufficient for the only divergence this change can produce, an older build over-reporting an entry a newer one suppresses. It is not sufficient to tell the reader of a single old report that an acknowledgement exists at all; what covers that is the acknowledgement log itself, which the snapshot ships beside the memo and which is readable without any tetel build.

The plain `look <path>` and `look --lines A:B` paths must be left alone by this design, because in `look_path` the returned bytes and the captured `output` are the same value `shown`; bounding the return there would necessarily change what is captured, which the ticket puts out of scope. `look_grep` is bounded and `look_path` is not, and that asymmetry is a consequence of the code's shape, not an oversight.

prop: Per-citation attribution is folded into the acknowledgement only as far as it honestly can be, which is not far. `NON_COVERAGE`'s last entry already states that whether a block's wording was ever examined against an earlier-settled co-citation is never answered by any listing, and the acknowledgement does not answer it either: the ack is per block, its key merely records every cited claim's digest, and the only place a per-citation judgement can appear is inside the author's verbatim `--why`, which the tool must not parse. The design's contribution is therefore to print the block's cited claim ids beside that verbatim reason in the acknowledged bullet, so a reader can pair the author's own words to the citations, and to leave the non-coverage entry standing.

This design neither settles nor depends on TET-61's separate question of warning an author at `prose --revise` time. It changes only the economics of that question: today such a warning could name no act, since the workspace verbs are create and revise and neither discharges anything, whereas afterwards it could name the ack verb. Whether the warning is worth building remains a measurement question this memo does not answer.

There is no act that gets an author the rest of a bounded census, and this design does not add one. Narrowing the root or the pattern is not available as a remedy, because a census is "one search of the whole worktree for the symbol itself" and a narrowed search stops qualifying as one; `look --grep` takes no other parameter that could page or filter. What remains available is an additional search rooted at a subdirectory, recorded as its own observation alongside the census rather than in place of it — and, outside the return path entirely, the per-file `GrepMatch` entries, which hold every matched line and ship complete into the snapshot.

The pin's non-stationarity is relocated rather than removed, and the relocation is the improvement. Measured on a scratch tree: rendering a second memo into it, changing no source, left the matched output of a search for the same symbol byte-identical while changing the emitted exclusion list from one rendered-memo pattern to two. So the captured output is now stationary against tetel's own churn — which was the ticket's within-run complaint, since an evidence ledger growing during grading no longer reaches the search at all — but the exclusion set is not, and because the design writes that set into the search record's label and the label is inside the pin, two censuses of the same symbol against the same source will still pin differently across a render. The difference is that the cause is now written in plain text in the same record, instead of being an invisible change in what the search happened to read.
